name: Areostationary Orbit
story: The Mars equivalent of geostationary — 17,031 km up, where an orbit takes exactly one Martian sidereal day (24 h 37 min 22 s), so a spacecraft would hang motionless over a fixed Martian longitude. No spacecraft has ever used this orbit. It's the design target for future Mars relay constellations: as crewed missions and surface bases grow, parking communications satellites in areostationary slots would mirror Earth's GEO comsat network, eliminating the daily comms outages that today's low-orbit relays impose on every surface mission.
comparison: Just below Mars's outer moon Deimos (23,460 km). Three areostationary satellites spaced 120° apart would cover the entire Martian disc — the same trick GEO comsats use for Earth broadcast TV.
